entities.summary: Francesco Zabarella was an Italian cardinal and canonist who played a pivotal role in shaping the Catholic Church's legal framework during the late Middle Ages. Born in unknown circumstances, Zabarella rose through the ranks of the Church, eventually becoming a cardinal in 1370. His most notable contribution was the codification of canon law, which he accomplished through his work on the Corpus Juris Canonici. This monumental work, completed in 1479, systematized the Church's legal principles and provided a comprehensive framework for its governance. Zabarella's efforts had a lasting impact on the Church's organization and jurisprudence, influencing the development of Western law and canon. The codification of canon law also facilitated the growth of universities and the emergence of a professional clergy. Despite his significant contributions, Zabarella's life remains shrouded in mystery, with his exact birth and death dates unknown. However, his legacy as a key figure in the history of the Catholic Church continues to be felt today.
